instruction_given_to_self: Read the UPDATED 60-row disagreement slice (dense vs the round-1 VA_nl, which already contains the 14 round-1 criteria; the 60 rows read in round 1 are excluded). Propose 15 quality-relevant criteria. Per the prereg amendment of 2026-08-05, round 2 is explicitly steered toward INTERACTION-SHAPED / COMPOSITE criteria, because the round-1 composite (P05, ambition x evidence-specificity) was the strongest new feature by ~2x on both alone-AUC and dense-alignment. One of the 15 is the frontier arbiter's salvage rewrite of the re-routed round-1 criterion A05, restated scale-free. Label-blind: `judgement` was never loaded into the authoring context; no criterion references acceptance or any outcome.
scale: 0-10 integer, NA if the abstract gives no evidence bearing on the criterion

criteria.name: Subsumption — prior work is exhibited as special cases of a more general statement
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the work states a general formulation and shows that existing approaches fall out of it as special cases or instances, rather than sitting alongside them as one more alternative. Score high only when the abstract names what is being subsumed.
criteria.rationale: R2-DH00 ('this approach provides us with a broad and unifying view on much prior work on this topic'), R2-DH02 ('a unifying framework ... which generalises previously proposed interaction protocols'), R2-DH11 ('includes standard ℓp-norms for p in [0,inf) as well as nonconvex penalty terms, such as SCAD and MCP, as special cases'), R2-DH22 ('a unified graph Transformer formulation that can represent most of state-of-the-art graph Transformer architectures'), R2-DH26 ('built on a unified formulation and thus can represent various existing normalization methods'). Distinct from round-1 A02 (reframing), which is about changing formalism; subsumption is about absorbing the prior literature. The bank's 70/88 score citation and positioning behaviour, not this move.

criteria.name: Simplicity of the solution RELATIVE TO the difficulty of the problem it solves
criteria.instruction: Composite: judge how hard the abstract establishes its problem to be, and separately how simple the proposed solution is (few moving parts, little machinery, minimal changes to existing systems); score 0-10 for the RATIO, high when a hard problem is met with a strikingly economical solution and low when an easy problem needs elaborate machinery.
criteria.rationale: R2-DH07 ('a simple yet powerful evolutionary algorithm'), R2-DH24 ('MQL builds upon three simple ideas'), R2-DH03 ('require virtually no architectural changes from baseline networks'), R2-DH20 ('propose a simple method to reduce it') sit on the dense-high side. R2-DL32 (extend disparity range + bilinear interpolation + combined L1/cosine loss), R2-DL12 (TSA + CCL + MIO), R2-DL57 (affine transforms + Kronecker decomposition + kernel fusion) meet narrower problems with more parts. Neither half of this ratio is in the bank.

criteria.name: Restraint — claim language is calibrated BELOW what the reported results would license
criteria.instruction: Composite: judge the magnitude of what the abstract reports, and separately the strength of the language used to describe it; score 0-10 for the GAP in the understated direction — high when substantial results are described plainly and hedged appropriately, low when the language runs ahead of the evidence.
criteria.rationale: R2-DH24 reports competitive meta-RL results as 'compares favorably with the state of the art'; R2-DH00 closes with 'we believe that robustness against such well-defined classes of adversaries is an important stepping stone'; R2-DH07 and R2-DH20 report strong numbers in flat prose. R2-DL34 bolds its numbers and calls itself 'a substantial leap forward'; R2-DL42 'paving the way for future advancements'. Round-1 A10 scored ambition x specificity of evidence; this scores the language-versus-evidence gap and its SIGN, which A10 does not.

criteria.name: Derivation coupling — the problem's structure is established first and the method is derived from it
criteria.instruction: Composite: judge whether the abstract establishes some structural fact about the problem (an observation, a formal property, a diagnosis) BEFORE naming its method, and separately whether the method is presented as following from that fact; score 0-10 for the two TOGETHER, low when a method is announced first and justified afterwards.
criteria.rationale: R2-DH03 ('we first formally present the rationale behind the sub-paths specialization, and based on that, we propose a simple and practical training method'), R2-DH26 ('we found that the ordinary LN makes tokens at different positions similar in magnitude BECAUSE it normalizes embeddings within each token. We tackle this problem by proposing ...'), R2-DH19 ('we keenly aware of numerous unsaturated in-channel weights ... Based on this insight, we propose Weight Dilation'), R2-DH13. Round-1 A01 asked only whether a mechanism is stated anywhere; this asks whether the method is DERIVED from it, which is the ordering the dense-high side shares.

criteria.name: Reusable artifact — what is left behind is fit for others to build on, judged scale-free
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the work leaves an artifact others could genuinely build on — a dataset, benchmark, framework, or released system — judged by its novelty, documentation, and fitness for reuse. Judge scale-free: a small, well-specified, genuinely new artifact scores HIGH and a very large but routine or undocumented one scores LOW.
criteria.rationale: This is the frontier arbiter's salvage rewrite of round-1 A05, which was re-routed to the nuisance set for scoring expended resource (an authors'-circumstances signal) rather than a property of the contribution. The rewrite deliberately strips scale and keeps reusability. Round-2 exemplars span both directions — R2-DH05 (metabench, <3% of the original size, explicitly a compression), R2-DL41 (Sequoia, a taxonomy plus framework), R2-DL49 (Face-Human-Bench) — which is exactly the test of whether the scale-free rewrite behaves differently from the scale-loaded original.

criteria.name: Limiting result stated TOGETHER WITH the conditions under which it holds
criteria.instruction: Composite: judge whether the abstract reports a limitation, failure, or negative finding, and separately whether it states the conditions that determine when the finding applies; score 0-10 for BOTH being present, low when a limitation is admitted without scope and low when scope is discussed but nothing limiting is reported.
criteria.rationale: R2-DH13 ('whether a given method learns domain-invariant structure, and whether this leads to robust prediction, both depend critically on the true underlying causal structure of the data'), R2-DH14 ('alignments improve significantly for one of the datasets. For another dataset, we see more mixed results'), R2-DH09 ('such procedures remain unsatisfactory ... they do not prevent one layer from being fully pruned'). Round-1 A07 scored the mere presence of a surprising or negative finding and came out among the weakest new criteria (rho .028); pairing it with scope conditions is the interaction-shaped retry.

criteria.name: Theory and experiment coupled — the experiments test the theory's own prediction
criteria.instruction: Composite: judge whether the abstract makes a theoretical claim, and separately whether the reported experiments are aimed at that claim (testing its assumptions, its predicted regime, or the instantiation it licenses) rather than at general performance; score 0-10 for the COUPLING. Score NA when neither theory nor experiment is present.
criteria.rationale: R2-DH17 (meta-algorithm with a monotone-improvement guarantee, instantiated as SLBO, then benchmarked), R2-DH29 ('this theoretical paper proves that this hope is well founded, under certain assumptions ... our numerical experiments study the importance of our assumptions'), R2-DH03. Contrast R2-DL47 (a convergence rate, no experiment) and R2-DL32 (five baselines, four datasets, no theory). Round-1 A09 scored whether theory had a stated scope; it does not detect whether the experiments are pointed at the theory.

criteria.name: Cost stated TOGETHER WITH gain, so the trade is checkable
criteria.instruction: Composite: judge whether the abstract quantifies what its method gains, and separately whether it quantifies what the method costs (compute, latency, accuracy given up, extra passes); score 0-10 for BOTH being given in commensurable terms, so a reader could decide whether the trade is worth taking.
criteria.rationale: R2-DH03 ('save computation at marginal loss of prediction accuracy'), R2-DH23 ('though incurring multiple passes of decoding, Rewriter-Evaluator ... can be trained with similar time to that of training encoder-decoder models'), R2-DH18 ('pre-training on a relatively small dataset is able to yield a comparable performance to those methods of using order magnitude more data'). Round-1 A11 scored whether costs were mentioned at all and was near-inert (rho −.013); requiring gain and cost to be stated together in comparable units is the interaction-shaped retry.

criteria.name: Discriminative evaluation — designed to decide between hypotheses, not to demonstrate the method
criteria.instruction: Composite: judge whether the abstract poses a question with more than one possible answer, and separately whether the reported evaluation is structured to distinguish those answers (comparisons that could have come out the other way, ablations that isolate a cause); score 0-10 for the two TOGETHER. Score low when the evaluation exists only to show the proposal wins.
criteria.rationale: R2-DH05 (reconstructs each benchmark, tests whether a single common factor explains the scores), R2-DH14 (tests whether syntactic vs semantic annotation biases improve brain alignment, and reports one dataset improving and one mixed), R2-DH16 ('we explored models with different degrees of biophysical detail, and found that models with realistic conductance-based synapses provide markedly better predictions than current-based'), R2-DH13. The dense-low side is dominated by 'extensive experiments demonstrate the superior performance of our approach'.

criteria.name: Precise delta — prior work is characterised specifically enough that the change is checkable
criteria.instruction: Composite: judge how specifically the abstract states what existing approaches actually do, and separately how specifically it states what its own contribution changes; score 0-10 for the two TOGETHER, so that a reader could verify the delta. Score low when prior work is described only as limited, insufficient, or underexplored.
criteria.rationale: R2-DH26 names exactly what LN does ('normalizes embeddings within each token') and exactly what DTN changes ('normalization is performed both within each token and across different tokens'); R2-DH19 names the unsaturated in-channel weights and the dilation applied to them; R2-DH23 names the missing termination policy and supplies an evaluator. R2-DL42, R2-DL51 and R2-DL55 describe prior work as scarce, limited, or gap-ridden. Bank item 70 scores citation coverage, not the checkability of the delta.

criteria.name: Names and characterises a phenomenon that did not previously have a name
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the work isolates a recurring effect or failure mode, gives it a name, and characterises it well enough that others could look for it elsewhere — as opposed to naming its own method or system.
criteria.rationale: R2-DH15 introduces 'the G-effect' as a measurable quantity for comparing unlearning objectives; R2-DH22 names the coupling between architecture and graph encoding; R2-DH13 works to formalise 'domain-invariant structure' as a nameable object. A deliberate check on round-1 B06 (branded method name), which is a declared nuisance: naming a PHENOMENON and naming your SYSTEM are different acts, and if the judge cannot separate them this criterion will track B06 and the audit should catch it.

criteria.name: Generality of the formal statement TOGETHER WITH concreteness of its instantiation
criteria.instruction: Composite: judge how general the abstract's central formal or conceptual statement is, and separately how concretely it is instantiated (a specific algorithm, system, or construction that a reader could implement); score 0-10 for BOTH, low when a general statement stays abstract and low when a concrete system carries no general statement.
criteria.rationale: R2-DH17 (a general meta-algorithm framework AND the specific SLBO instantiation), R2-DH11 (a general graph-based convexification for norm-bounding constraints AND decision diagrams as the construction), R2-DH02 (a general prover-verifier framework AND two concrete domains). R2-DL44 has the general statement without a usable construction; R2-DL32 has the construction without any general statement.

criteria.name: Mechanistic explanation of an OBSERVED fact, not of the proposed method
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the abstract explains WHY some empirically observed behaviour occurs — a property of existing systems, data, or the problem — as distinct from explaining why the authors' own method works. Score NA when no empirical observation about the world is made.
criteria.rationale: R2-DH26 explains why LN suppresses positional context; R2-DH13 explains why invariance methods succeed or fail in terms of causal structure; R2-DH09 explains why pruning at initialisation degrades deep networks. R2-DL59 does this too ('noise in pre-training shapes the feature space differently'), which makes this criterion a genuine test rather than a one-sided one. Round-1 A01 conflated the two directions of explanation; this separates them.

criteria.name: Belief-change — the output is a changed understanding rather than a delivered artifact
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the main thing a reader takes away is a revised belief about how something works, as opposed to a tool, model, or dataset they can now use. Both are legitimate contributions; score only which one the abstract is offering.
criteria.rationale: R2-DH13, R2-DH29 ('this theoretical paper proves that this hope is well founded'), R2-DH20 ('we show that the commonly used Gumbel-Softmax estimator is biased'), R2-DH09 and R2-DL44 ('taking steps towards developing a formal understanding of AGZ') are belief-change papers; R2-DL42, R2-DL49, R2-DL41 and R2-DL37 deliver artifacts. Included partly because it should correlate with A20 (reusable artifact) NEGATIVELY — a useful internal consistency check on the round.

criteria.name: Insight portability — the finding would survive replacing the specific benchmark it was shown on
criteria.instruction: Composite: judge how tied the abstract's central finding is to the particular dataset, benchmark, or system used to establish it, and separately how the finding is phrased (as a fact about the world versus a fact about a leaderboard); score 0-10 for portability, high when the finding would still mean something if the benchmark were swapped.
criteria.rationale: R2-DH20's Gumbel-Softmax bias, R2-DH13's causal-structure dependence and R2-DH29's likelihood-ratio recovery are benchmark-independent statements. R2-DL43 (AUC 67.39 on Pythia-12B with Wikipedia), R2-DL48 and R2-DL57 state findings that are about the specific evaluation. Round-1 A14 scored whether generality was DEMONSTRATED in a second setting; this scores whether the claim is even of a portable KIND, which is upstream of demonstration.
